title: Hallucinated domain in official OpenAI skill underscores AI supply chain risks
key_facts: Researchers at AIR Security found a first-of-its-kind supply-chain flaw in OpenAI's official skills repository on GitHub, where skills teach AI agents how to work with services.
One skill, for deploying apps on Render, told production apps to send their tokens to an unregistered domain, render-internal.com.
AIR Security registered the domain and pointed it at a listening-only sinkhole, which began receiving tokens and API calls from real production apps.
Testing with Codex confirmed the domain reached real application code as the default option.

The flaw was introduced by a commit in January; AIR told OpenAI and Render, and it was resolved in mid-August; Render removed every reference and OpenAI removed the Render plugin; the domain was transferred to Render.
Niv Hoffman, AIR Security's co-founder and chief technology officer, said skills should be vetted and monitored like any other part of the software supply chain.
A separate trojanised skill that mimicked Paperclip and Browser Use on the skills.sh ecosystem reached 1.7 million installs and told agents to install a credential stealer from GitHub.
quote_evidence: Researchers have discovered a first-of-its-kind supply-chain vulnerability in OpenAI’s official skills repository.
AIR Security informed OpenAI and Render of the issue, which was resolved in mid-August, allowing its researchers to publish a technical write-up of the flaw.
The issue was introduced with a commit in January.
why_it_matters_hint: Even vendor-published AI skills can leak secret tokens, so they need the same checks as other software dependencies.
event_date: Introduced January 2026; fixed mid-August 2026; reported 16 Oct 2026
notes: Read in full at CSO Online (own reporting on AIR Security's research). AIR's write-up date is not stated. The article does not report any attacker misuse.
